desk_read: Energy and metals markets diverged sharply yesterday as complex-wide positioning shifts played out against active expiry rolls. WTI Crude Oil climbed +2.35% with total open interest changing by +3.0k contracts (+0.3%) in backwardation, while Brent (NYMEX) gained +2.42% with open interest up +103 contracts (+0.1%) also in backwardation. Meanwhile, severe long liquidation hit the metals space. Gold tumbled -2.45% alongside a -9.2k contract (-2.5%) drop in total open interest, Copper plunged -4.70% with open interest down -16.2k contracts (-5.2%), and Silver dropped -5.54% as total open interest fell -1.4k contracts (-1.2%), all settling in contango. In equities, Nasdaq 100 fell -1.99% with a +2.5k contract (+0.8%) increase in total open interest pointing to new shorts.
oil_read: Yesterday, WTI (CLF27) rose +2.35% with total open interest up +3.0k contracts (+0.3%) and volume at 1.1x its 20-day average, while Brent (BZG27) gained +2.42% with total open interest up +103 contracts (+0.1%) and volume at 0.8x its 20-day average, both flows being too small to read as a flow. Both markets remain in backwardation, with the CLF27-CLM27 spread at +5.33 $/bbl and BZG27-BZM27 at +6.64 $/bbl, and Brent-WTI for F27 at +9.35 $/bbl.
bias_read: WTI Crude Oil and Brent (NYMEX) show a mildly bullish bias with backwardation, where the curve steepening in Brent warns of a potential squeeze rather than a confirmed trend. Gold and Silver display a mildly bearish bias driven by long liquidation with heavy volume at 1.6x the 20-day average and 1.9x the 20-day average, meaning the selling lacks strong structural conviction. Nasdaq 100 features a mildly bearish bias with new shorts on volume at 1.2x the 20-day average, signaling emerging downside pressure. Across the desk, the overall picture reveals fragile upside momentum in energy contrasted with active liquidation and fresh short positioning in metals and equities.
